manuscript_inserted_text: \revminor{These eleven candidates comprised the non-target meteorological variables available in the original ERA5 extract. They describe complementary aspects of the atmospheric and surface state: near-surface temperature and moisture conditions (t2m and d2m), wind and pressure conditions (u10, v10 and sp), cloud cover (tcc), surface radiative and moisture exchanges (ssr and e, where e is the modelled actual evaporation rather than potential evaporation), and recent precipitation characteristics (lsp, mxtpr and mntpr). Previous data-driven rainfall prediction studies have considered observational analogues of temperature, dew point, wind, pressure, cloud cover and solar radiation, although these are not necessarily identical to the ERA5 fields used here \citep{manandhar2019data,rahman2022rainfall,gao2025applying}. The precipitation-related variables lsp, mxtpr and mntpr instead provide information about preceding-hour large-scale precipitation and the within-hour extrema of total precipitation rate \citep{ecmwf_era5_documentation}. The inclusion of all eleven variables defines an exploratory candidate pool rather than presupposing that each variable contributes independent predictive information; their associations with the forecast target were subsequently examined through training-period screening and lead-time diagnostics.}
